key_insight: A feedforward neural network using the writhe density matrix can classify the first six prime two-component links with high accuracy, showing that this geometric descriptor encodes topology-relevant information.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a fast surrogate for exact topological invariant calculations, which could be useful for analyzing polymer, DNA, and protein link structures in large-scale simulations.
method: Compute the writhe density matrix from polymer/link configurations
Train a feedforward neural network on thermally equilibrated samples
Test robustness across temperature, component length, and Gaussian noise
evidence_signal: The model achieves 97% classification accuracy on thermally equilibrated configurations and remains strong across temperatures and link lengths, but degrades sharply under topology-altering Gaussian noise.
watch_item: Performance may drop when inputs are perturbed in ways that alter topology, so the method should not be assumed robust to noisy or unresolved geometric data.
paper_title: Writhe-Based Polymer Link Classification Using Machine Learning
